title: Farid's ship is late
body: Farid is a merchant your house knows. His ship is late, and he cannot pay his debts this season. He asks you for 5 until it comes in.

choices.label: Lend him the money
choices.hint: It costs 5 now and pays 4 in two seasons. Ships are often late. Some never come.

choices.label: Refuse
choices.hint: Farid will remember. The court likes a careful house.

note: Partners sometimes lent each other money. A loan was often an act of kindness, with no interest.

sources.at: pp. 317 and 327; loans between partners, and loans as acts of kindness

title: A friend asks for a loan
body: Murad has been your friend for years. His goods are stuck, and he needs 7 dinars for a few seasons. He does not ask for a paper. He says you would do the same for him.

choices.label: Lend him 7 dinars
choices.hint: It costs 7 dinars now and 4 come back in three seasons. He may not repay it all. He will remember.

choices.label: Say you cannot
choices.hint: Murad will ask someone else. The court likes a careful house.

note: In the Geniza papers, loans were often an act of kindness. Lending for interest was frowned on.

sources.at: p. 317; loans given as acts of charity, and interest shunned

title: Samir asks who pays the road
body: Samir could go to {to} with {good}. If you send him, he asks the house to pay his food, boats and gate fees on the way. He says the house should carry those costs.

choices.label: Let the house pay his costs
choices.hint: The house pays for the trip and keeps all the profit. The next sheet shows the cost. Agents hear of a house that pays.

choices.label: Tell him to pay from his own share
choices.hint: He keeps a third of the profit and pays his own way. Partners respect that. He will not forget it.

choices.label: Ask Samir to wait a season
choices.hint: Samir stays home and is not pleased. Partners like a house that thinks first.

note: In the Geniza papers, a traveller's living costs, transport and customs were commonly paid out of the shared money. Some contracts made the traveller pay them himself.

sources.at: pp. 325 to 326; the traveller's costs paid out of the partnership, or by himself

title: Dalal wants a bigger stall
body: Dalal sells cloth and wants a bigger stall. She cannot find a lender, because lending for a fee is frowned on. She asks you to be her partner for a year instead.

choices.label: Put in 5 dinars as her partner
choices.hint: It costs 5 dinars now and brings 4 in four seasons. You would take a share of the profit, and the whole market would see the partnership.

choices.label: Lend her 3 dinars as a kindness
choices.hint: A small help of 3 dinars now, and 3 come back in three seasons. She will repay it, and the street will hear of the kindness.

choices.label: Keep your money for your own trade
choices.hint: It stays free to work and gains 2 dinars in two seasons, and the court likes a careful house. Dalal may be hurt.

note: In the Geniza papers, partnerships did the work of loans at interest, which people avoided. One partner put in money, and the one who worked kept part of the profit.

sources.at: p. 317; partnership in the place of loans on interest

title: A share paid on paper
body: A trading house at Quseir offers you a share of its trade. It will pay you on paper, a written promise to pay later, not in coin. Many houses do this, and it is slow.

choices.label: Take the share and the paper
choices.hint: It costs 6 dinars now. The house pays in two seasons, and partners think you trust well.

choices.label: Ask to be paid in coin
choices.hint: It costs 8 dinars now. The house is glad of coin, and foreign houses hear of it.

choices.label: Decline the offer
choices.hint: It costs nothing. The house offers its trade to someone else.

note: Papers found at Quseir from 1215 to 1235 show that trade there ran mostly on credit, written on paper. That is about 100 years before 1324.

title: A share in a great ship
body: Jalal is a rich shipowner in Aden. He owns his ship and all its cargo, with no partners. He offers you a small share in his next voyage.

choices.label: Take a small share
choices.hint: It costs 10 dinars now. The voyage takes seasons, and foreign houses think well of you.

choices.label: Offer a qirad instead
choices.hint: It costs 14 dinars now. A qirad is a partnership: you give money and he does the trading. Partners think well of you.

choices.label: Decline, to be safe
choices.hint: It costs nothing. Jalal offers the share to someone else.

note: Ibn Battuta wrote that one merchant at Aden might own a great ship and its whole cargo. He had no partner, because of the huge capital he held.

sources.at: vol. 2, p. 372 (one merchant owning a great ship)
